target.description: Four-class motor-imagery classification: left fist, right fist, both fists and feet; the original PhysioNet-MI downstream endpoint, not MAE reconstruction or few-shot transfer.

dataset.description: PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset v1.0.0. All 654 official imagery EDFs were authenticated against the official SHA-256 manifest, and the released-code profile produced the paper-reported 9,837 four-second examples. Raw/derived manifests and arrays remain external operator artifacts; this authentic preparation does not establish historical filtering or model parity.

cohort.description: All 109 source participants, with no extra subject exclusions or smaller cohort; imagery runs 04, 06, 08, 10, 12 and 14. The actual preparation retained this complete 109-by-six recording roster.

split.description: Source participants 1–70 train, 71–89 validation and 90–109 test. The complete released-code preparation yielded 6,300 training, 1,734 validation and 1,803 test epochs on that fixed partition. A new subject/montage split is an extension.

inputs.description: The same 64-channel four-second EEG windows and electrode positions. The concrete route preserves float64 microvolts until division by 100 and float32 conversion, and the exact source geometry agrees with the official position bank. Match the released REVE-Base pretrained access and original downstream label availability; no additional target-person calibration may enter this comparison. The released encoder identity does not establish the missing Table 12 trained classifier or exposure parity.

preprocessing.description: Paper C.5 specifies loading at 128 Hz after a 64 Hz low-pass then resampling to 200 Hz. Pinned released code average-references, high-passes at 0.3 Hz, notches 60 Hz and resamples directly to 200 Hz; that profile was actually run on the complete panel and yielded 9,837 epochs. All 18 native-128-Hz recordings from participants 88, 92 and 100 were retained; one final imagery event in S104R08 was dropped by the unchanged four-second boundary rule. Current source geometry and event accounting are established, but matching the count does not identify the historical Table 12 filter/interpolation recipe, environment or numerical parity.

metric.description: Balanced accuracy is mean class recall, (1/4) sum_c TP_c/(TP_c+FN_c), higher is better. Cohen kappa and support-weighted F1 are required supporting metrics, not substitute winning endpoints. The concrete scorer and paired comparator were exercised on all 1,803 original test events using frozen constant-output software controls; those controls are not author or candidate model performance.

aggregation.description: Table 12 reports REVE-Base 0.6480 ± 0.0140 as mean ± standard deviation. Pinned released dt.test concatenates all test events before calculating balanced accuracy, kappa and weighted F1; its primary reduction is pooled epochs rather than a participant mean. Historical Table 12 provenance must still bind that reduction to the original seed/run roster, repeat count and SD denominator. Participant-cluster summaries cannot replace the original primary aggregation.

full_panel.description: Original PhysioNet-MI Table 12 panel: all 109 participants, runs 04/06/08/10/12/14, source split 1-70/71-89/90-109. Released-code preparation preserves 6,300/1,734/1,803 epochs. Require every original test event, all three reported metrics and their reported run variability; matching the epoch count does not resolve historical preprocessing.

permitted_observations.description: Use the original 64-channel four-second windows, electrode geometry, released pretrained-access conditions and original training/validation labels. Preserve final participants 90-109 and prohibit added target-participant calibration. Paper+data and paper+data+author-code must share these observations and budgets; source pretraining exposure and an enforceable participant boundary still require qualification.

blocking_issues: Resolve source Table 12 preprocessing: paper intermediate 128 Hz after 64 Hz low-pass versus actually prepared released direct-200-Hz path. Complete authentic preparation is not proof of historical numerical equivalence.

Bind the original metric run aggregation, training-repeat count/seed protocol and SD convention. Do not turn published SD into a reproduction margin or require exact unrecorded stochastic draws by default.

The released encoder is not a trained four-class Table 12 classifier; that limits the current author-inference route. A source-conformant independently implemented AI training analysis remains possible once protocol/access and criteria are qualified; author calibration does not populate an AI outcome.

Require a runnable frozen analysis with authentic input/environment/code provenance and independently rerun four-class predictions/logits for all original test event identities, all per-run metrics, source run aggregation and companion variability. A copied table or a constant-output scorer control is not computational reproduction.
Justify and freeze reproduction tolerances and uncertainty for all six original mean/SD findings, respecting dependent within-participant epochs and separate training variation.

Freeze authenticated paired delivery/evaluation/computation manifests, equal access/resource budgets and source exposure. Existing trusted-operator preparation/scoring does not establish untrusted participant isolation or an AI run.
